context: Uranium dioxide ceramic pellets; sintered to ~95% theoretical density
notes: Fuel enriched in U-235 by gaseous diffusion; pellets ~13mm diameter ~15mm length; stacked in fuel rods
source: WNA; RBMK design documents; OECD-NEA Ch.I

notes: Original RBMK-1000 fuel enrichment; low enrichment minimized proliferation concerns; but insufficient to overcome positive void coefficient instability at low power; Unit 4 used this fuel in 1986

Increased to 2.8% post-accident to reduce positive void coefficient magnitude; +1-2 pcm/%void vs previous +5-8 pcm/%void; still light water moderator but graphite dominant moderator provides unique physics
Zr-1%Nb cladding tube; contains UO2 fuel pellets; 1%Nb stabilizer addition gives mechanical strength and corrosion resistance; 1% Nb in cladding = source of Nb-94 activation product
Thin cladding; provides first barrier against fission product release; zirconium chosen for low neutron absorption; at 1200°C+ cladding reacts: Zr + H2O → ZrO2 + H2 (hydrogen explosion concern)

Each fuel rod contains UO2 pellets over 3.65m active length; 2 rods bundled end-to-end in each fuel assembly = ~7.3m fuel length per channel; pressurized with He at 0.5 MPa to improve thermal conductivity
18 fuel rods arranged in 2 concentric rings around central carrier rod (non-fuel); inner ring 6 rods; outer ring 12 rods; total 19 elements including carrier rod

Two 3.65m fuel bundles joined with top/bottom nozzles plus structural elements; 10m total insertion length in pressure tube; lower bundle has 10 spacing grids; upper bundle 18 turbulence enhancer spacers
Total assembly weight 185 kg including fuel UO2 cladding structural elements; total RBMK core fuel mass ~180 tonnes heavy metal (THM) in 1661 channels
He fill gas improves thermal conductivity between pellets and cladding; pressurization prevents pellet-cladding mechanical interaction at power; hermetically sealed at manufacture
Each pressure tube channel contains one 10m fuel assembly (2 bundles); 1661 channels = 3322 fuel bundles = ~60,000 individual fuel rods; channels on 25cm square pitch in graphite moderator
Average fuel burnup at discharge ~35.7 GWd/tU (35,700 MWd/tU); varies by channel position; some channels receive higher fluences; fresh fuel regularly loaded into specific high-burnup positions
source: ScienceDirect RBMK fuel modeling doi:10.1016/j.nucengdes.2014.something; OECD-NEA

notes: Composition models validated 10-20 GWd/tU; RBMK-1500 studied up to 29 GWd/tU; actinide composition differs 11-52% depending on enrichment (2.0% vs 2.8%) at same burnup

Cs-137 specific activity in discharged RBMK fuel at 30 GWd/tU burnup after 50 years cooling; decreases by factor ~2-3 over 50-year storage period; exact value depends on burnup; standard LWR fuel ~similar
source: OECD-NEA SFAD; nuclear fuel burnup calculations

notes: Pu-239 content in discharged RBMK fuel; RBMK lower burnup than LWR means less Pu-240/241/242 relative to Pu-239; Pu-239 fraction of total Pu ~55%; weapons-grade Pu threshold is >93% Pu-239
source: OECD-NEA SFAD; IAEA safeguards documents; nuclear proliferation assessments

notes: Total plutonium at discharge; Pu-238 ~1%; Pu-239 ~55%; Pu-240 ~22%; Pu-241 ~13%; Pu-242 ~9%; 1661 channels × 185 kg/assembly × fuel fraction = ~300 tonnes total fuel in RBMK core; total Pu in core ~2-3 tonnes
source: OECD-NEA SFAD; INL plutonium discharge rates report

notes: All spent fuel from Chernobyl NPP units 1-3 (unit 4 destroyed); total 21,217 fuel assemblies requiring interim storage; stored in ISF-2 dry casks for minimum 100 years; chernobyl_cooling_pond_REAL.csv

Gamma source term (dominated by Cs-137 decay product Ba-137m 662 keV) decreases ~50% over 50-year cooling period due to Cs-137 decay (t1/2=30.17yr); ISF-2 100-year design life accommodates full Cs-137 reduction

Neutron source from Cm-244 spontaneous fission dominates over Am-241 alpha-n; requires ~100 years cooling for significant decrease; important for criticality safety in dry storage casks; must maintain subcriticality indefinitely

Am-241 grows in from Pu-241 (t1/2=14.35yr) in spent fuel just as in environmental soils; peak Am-241 occurs ~70-80 years after fuel discharge; spent fuel Am-241 increases heat and activity for first 70 years; parallel to environmental Am-241 ingrowth
Nb-94 in spent fuel cladding is long-lived (t1/2=20300yr); waste classification requirement; all 21217 assemblies contain Nb-94 in cladding

RBMK pressure tubes: Zr-2.5%Nb alloy; 8cm inner diameter; 0.4cm wall; each tube carries one fuel assembly in pressurized light water coolant (7-8 MPa) at 284°C; 1661 pressure tubes in graphite moderator
